note: Phase 10A Section 13: GPU memory-pressure test, SmolLM2-360M, Vulkan (NVIDIA GTX 1650, 4096 MiB total, ~3956 MiB free at test time), --gpu-layers auto (MEMBRANE's own real policy engine, not forced).
device: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650, 4096 MiB total VRAM

runs.result: FAILED CLOSED -- 0 layers fit (est. KV alone = 5GB > 4GB total VRAM)
partial offload -- 1 layer stays on CPU
partial offload -- q4 itself now hits its own real boundary, degrades gracefully rather than failing

findings: At ctx=131072, native fails completely (fail-closed, exit 5, no silent CPU fallback -- existing MEMBRANE behavior, unaffected by Phase 10A).
At the same ctx=131072, q8 fits but only 31/32 layers -- one layer forced to CPU.
At the same ctx=131072, q4 fits with all 32/32 layers fully GPU-resident.
Across ctx 131072-220000, q8 fails completely (0 layers fit) while q4 keeps all 32 layers on GPU the entire range -- a real, substantial usable-context extension, not a marginal one.

q4's own boundary is real too: at ctx=260000 it drops to 23/32 layers (partial offload, not failure) -- MEMBRANE's fail-closed/graceful-degradation policy behaves correctly for q4 exactly as it already does for q8/native, no special-casing needed.
conclusion: CONFIRMED (Section 13's central question): on this GPU/model, Q4 KV allows both (a) more layers to remain GPU-resident than Q8 at a fixed context, and (b) a substantially larger usable context range under full GPU residency than either Q8 or native support at all. This is likely the most operationally significant Phase 10A result -- it is not just a memory accounting win, it changes what configurations are even runnable on this class of GPU.
